name: Dropshipping and social-commerce sellers (Instagram, TikTok, Facebook)
sector: 7.M Digital economy, social and public sector

problems.words: Orders come in DMs, comments and WhatsApp and I lose track
quick_ideas: Move each order into one list the moment it is confirmed, not at night
Ask comment buyers to message you, so orders sit in one place.

workzap_build.text: a WhatsApp order flow where buyers choose item, size and colour, and every confirmed order lands in one list automatically.

problems.ask_first: Which place do most of the lost orders come from, direct messages, comments or WhatsApp?
problems.free_stops: The order flow and catalogue set-up are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count today’s confirmed orders against parcels actually booked by evening, so you see how many enquiries fall through the cracks.
Give one staff member the job of writing every confirmed order into one notebook immediately, so packing starts from one place.

problems.words: Hundreds of "price?" messages and most never buy
quick_ideas: Show price and sizes on the post itself, so the question isn't needed
Point enquiries to your WhatsApp catalogue instead of typing details each time.

workzap_build.text: an automatic first reply with price, sizes and an order link, so you only handle serious buyers.

problems.ask_first: Roughly what share of those price messages come from live sales or posts, and how many are repeat askers?
problems.free_stops: The reply flow and its wording are prepared in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which products trigger the most price messages this week, so you know where unclear posts are wasting reply time.
Give one person one daily slot to answer price enquiries from one written product list, so replies stay quick and consistent.

problems.words: Supplier says it's available, then it's out after I take payment
quick_ideas: Confirm availability with the supplier before accepting an advance
Ask the supplier for a daily stock update, so you sell what exists.

workzap_build.text: a stock sheet shared with your supplier, showing what is available before you take payment.

problems.ask_first: Does this happen with one supplier mostly, or with several, and how often in a week?
problems.free_stops: How the supplier updates it and how it links to orders is covered in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare supplier availability claims with what was actually fillable this week, so unreliable items stop soaking up your chat time.
Give one person the job of marking each supplier item available or out in one notebook each morning, so payments are taken more carefully.

problems.words: I don't know if the supplier actually dispatched
quick_ideas: Ask the supplier to send the tracking number per order the same day
Check once each evening for orders with no tracking number yet.

workzap_build.text: a dispatch tracker with a tracking number per order and WhatsApp alerts when one is overdue.

problems.ask_first: Is it one supplier that goes quiet after payment, or most of them?
problems.free_stops: The tracker and alert rules are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count orders with payment confirmed but no dispatch proof by evening, so you see which supplier follow-ups are being missed.
Give one person one daily time to chase missing dispatch proof from one written list, so stuck orders move sooner.

problems.words: Checking payment screenshots against the bank app takes hours
quick_ideas: Check bank and wallet credits at two fixed times a day instead of per screenshot
Dispatch only once the credit shows, not the screenshot, which also stops fake ones.

workzap_build.text: an advance-payment log matching wallet and bank credits to orders and flagging unmatched screenshots.

problems.ask_first: Do most payments come by bank transfer, or through wallets like Easypaisa and JazzCash?
problems.free_stops: How credits are matched to orders is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many screenshots match real credits and how many do not this week, so the fraud pattern shows.
Give one person two fixed times to check incoming credits from one list of pending orders, so dispatch decisions stop interrupting the day.

problems.words: Customers refuse COD parcels after ordering in a live
quick_ideas: Confirm every live-sale order with the buyer before booking the courier
Note which products get refused most, so you know where to ask for an advance.

workzap_build.text: a live-sale order taker where buyers reply with item codes and every order is confirmed automatically before booking.

problems.ask_first: Do the refusals come mostly from live sales, or from ordinary posts as well?
problems.free_stops: The live-sale code system and confirmation steps go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count which live-sale items are refused most often this week, so you spot where excitement is not turning into delivery.
Give one person the job of confirming each live order from one written list before booking, so fewer parcels go nowhere.

problems.words: I boost posts but can't tell which ones sold
quick_ideas: Ask each buyer where they saw the item and note it with the order
Compare boost spend against delivered orders each week.

workzap_build.text: codes per post or boost tied to orders, showing which content actually sold.

problems.ask_first: Do you boost a few posts each week, or many, and do buyers usually say where they saw the item?
problems.free_stops: The code set-up and reporting are covered in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each delivered order beside the post or live it came from this week, so your useful promotions stop blending together.
Give one person one notebook for recording every order source at confirmation time, so sold items can be tied back to promotion effort.

problems.words: Pre-orders: no list of who's waiting for what
quick_ideas: Keep one waitlist by item and size with any advance taken
Contact the waitlist, with their permission, as soon as stock lands.

workzap_build.text: a pre-order waitlist that sends an "it's back" WhatsApp message automatically to buyers who asked.

problems.ask_first: Is the waiting list mostly in chats, or on paper, and how many items are pre-ordered at a time?
problems.free_stops: The waitlist and message flow are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many waiting buyers asked again for the same item this week, so the size of the pre-order backlog is clear.
Give one person one notebook page per item for waiting buyers and advances, so arrivals can be matched without confusion.

problems.words: Everything is on my phone — if it's lost, the business is gone
quick_ideas: Turn on chat backup today
Keep a copy of your order list somewhere other than the phone.

workzap_build.text: order and buyer history kept safely in the cloud, off the phone.

problems.ask_first: Is your order list only in WhatsApp chats, or is it also written somewhere else?
problems.free_stops: Where and how records are stored is explained in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk through your current orders and note what exists only on the phone, so you see what would disappear if it failed.
Give one person a daily job of copying active orders into one notebook, so the business can still run during phone trouble.

problems.words: I don't know my real profit after courier, returns and boosting
quick_ideas: Work out once what one order of your best sellers really leaves after courier, returns and boosting
Recheck supplier prices, since they often rise quietly.

workzap_build.text: a per-order profit view with a weekly WhatsApp summary of orders, delivered, returned and cash pending.

problems.ask_first: Which cost do you least know, the courier, the returns or the boosting?
problems.free_stops: The cost model and summary layout are prepared in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note one week of delivered, returned and cancelled orders beside courier and promotion spending, so your real profit leak is clearer.
Give one person the job of writing every order cost in one notebook daily, so profit stops being guessed.

problems.words: Can't take a day off — everything depends on me
quick_ideas: Hand one routine task, like courier booking, to a helper this week
Agree with helpers on how common questions are answered, so replies stay consistent.

workzap_build.text: a shared reply library and posting calendar with reminders, so helpers can run the routine without you.

problems.ask_first: Which job stops you most, answering buyers, booking couriers or dealing with suppliers?
problems.free_stops: The handover set-up and reply library are built in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many times staff ask you to approve routine work in one day, so your biggest handover gap stands out.
Give one helper one fixed hour to handle routine order updates from one written list, so you can step away briefly.

never_say: Promises of reach, followers, virality or sales.
Any health or beauty claims for slimming, herbal or skin products.
Help with buying followers, fake reviews, replica goods or copying other brands' content.
Tracking down, exposing or shaming a buyer who sent a fake screenshot.
Tax or registration advice — say "talk to an accountant"; never ask for page logins, OTPs or wallet PINs.

sample_reply.person: Mera Instagram page hai, orders DMs mein aate hain aur miss ho jate hain. Koi hal batayein.
sample_reply.pi: Ji haan, is ka hal mumkin hai aur shuruaat aaj se ho sakti hai. 1) Order confirm hote hi usi waqt ek list mein daal dein, raat ka intezar na karein. 2) Comments wale buyers ko message karne ka kahein, taake sab orders ek jagah rahein. Workzap yeh kaam aap ke liye automatically kar sakta hai: WhatsApp par order flow jahan buyer khud item, size aur colour chune aur har order khud ek list mein aa jaye. Kya main aap ke liye solution document aur quote banwa doon? Mana bhi kar sakte hain.
